price.quote: Priced at $2,699, the Electra Ponto Go! e-bike comes in four colors and one size.

cls.quote: The 78 lb (35 kg) Class 3 e-bike can hit speeds of up to 20 mph (32 km/h) on throttle-only control, or even higher speeds of up to 26 mph (42 km) in pedal assist.
cls.basis: 2023 launch spec (Class 3, 26 mph); current Ponto Go! is Class 2, so not counted

wh.quote: The bike also carries a rather large battery at 650Wh, which Electra claims offers a maximum range of 60 miles (96 km).
wh.basis: 2023 launch spec says 650Wh; differs from current 625Wh

range.quote: The bike also carries a rather large battery at 650Wh, which Electra claims offers a maximum range of 60 miles (96 km).

wt.quote: The 78 lb (35 kg) Class 3 e-bike can hit speeds of up to 20 mph (32 km/h) on throttle-only control

load.quote: This bike has a maximum total weight limit (combined weight of bicycle, rider, and cargo) of 440 pounds (199 kg).

motor.quote: That’s thanks to a powerful 750W hub motor in the rear, maxing out the legal limit for e-bike power in the US.

height.quote: Size	Rider Height ⟶ One size fits most | 4'11" - 6'10"
The company says that the bike can support riders in the height range of 4’10” to 6’2″ (147 to 188 cm) and has a payload capacity of 360 lb (163 kg).

notes: Maker link redirects to .../ponto-go/f/EF275/ponto-go%2521/59517/ (model 5341187). On sale at $1,999.93; original $2,699.99. Electrek is the Aug 2023 launch article, which describes a Class 3 / 26 mph / 650Wh bike; the current Ponto Go! is Class 2 / 20 mph / 625Wh (the Class 2/3 version is now the separate Ponto Go! S), so Electrek is used only for specs that match (price, motor, range) and listed for others as context. Rider height differs a lot: maker 4'11"-6'10" vs Electrek 4'10"-6'2" (2023). Electrek also gives a 360 lb payload (2023); maker gives 440 lb total. EBR has no Ponto Go! review.
